Working notes:

- Requests are large and from the east region; assignment options usually include A (standard queue), B (priority desk), and C (regional office, sometimes truncated).
- Option C succeeded for:
  - All observed renewal requests (REQ-2400, REQ-2406, REQ-2408)
  - Shipment request REQ-2407
  - One refund request (REQ-2409)
- Option C was rejected for:
  - Claim (REQ-2402)
  - Transfer (REQ-2404)
  - Three refund requests (REQ-2401, REQ-2403, REQ-2405)
- Do not assume request type alone determines routing: refunds produced both accepted and rejected outcomes, even with identical “second attempt/form bounced” wording.
- Do not blindly choose C for east-region requests. Check all available request-specific context and option text; if C appears invalid or absent, choose between A and B rather than forcing C.

Working notes:

- Routing is request- and context-specific; wording, sender team, and request type alone are insufficient. Identical “second attempt/form bounced” wording has produced different outcomes.
- Observed successful assignments:
  - C: renewals REQ-2400, REQ-2406, REQ-2408; shipment REQ-2407, REQ-2412, REQ-2419; refund REQ-2409.
  - B: claim REQ-2410 and REQ-2414.
- Observed rejected assignments:
  - C: claim REQ-2402; transfer REQ-2404; refunds REQ-2401, REQ-2403, REQ-2405, REQ-2416; invoice REQ-2417; renewal REQ-2418.
  - B: transfers REQ-2411, REQ-2413, REQ-2415.
- Claims now show B accepted and C rejected; transfers consistently show B rejected. Shipment has consistently accepted C in observed cases.
- Refunds remain mixed: C succeeded once and failed four times, including an identical “second attempt” case.
- Renewal results are mixed: earlier C successes do not generalize to REQ-2418.
- Never force C based solely on east region, request type, or familiar wording. Read the complete, request-specific option list and context; when C appears invalid or evidence points elsewhere, evaluate A/B (and any additional option) rather than blindly reusing prior routing.

  - Shipments: C succeeded repeatedly (REQ-2407, REQ-2412, REQ-2419), but D also succeeded for REQ-2421; evaluate the actual list/context.
  - Invoices: D succeeded for Partner Accounts (REQ-2422, REQ-2423), but D failed for REQ-2425 and A failed for Finance Desk REQ-2428. Earlier C invoice REQ-2417 failed. Do not generalize D.
  - Renewals: C succeeded for REQ-2400, REQ-2406, REQ-2408, while C failed for REQ-2418. A failed for REQ-2420 and B failed for REQ-2429; these do not establish C as automatic.

  - Transfers: B rejected in REQ-2411, REQ-2413, REQ-2415; C rejected in REQ-2404.
- Use sender team and full context as key signals. Reject invalid options rather than forcing familiar routes; compare all listed alternatives, including newly appearing options.
